ko: 어느 겨울밤, 기도실 촛불 아래서 확신이 흔들립니다. 정말 신은 당신을 택했을까요?
mt: One winter night, under a candle in the prayer room, I'm sure I'm shaking. Did God really choose you?
en: One winter night, beneath the prayer-room candles, your conviction wavers. Did God truly choose you?

ko: 꿈에서 신의 목소리를 들었다고 확신합니다. 아침 라디오가 잡음 속에서 노래를 흘립니다.
mt: I'm sure I heard God's voice in my dream, and the morning radio is singing in the noise.
en: You are certain you heard God's voice in a dream. The morning radio leaks a song through the static.

ko: 금식 기도를 결심했습니다. 부엌에서는 밥 짓는 냄새가 솔솔 올라옵니다.
mt: The smell of cooking in the kitchen comes up.
en: You resolve to fast and pray. From the kitchen drifts the smell of rice cooking.

ko: 당신이 존경하던 성직자가 추문에 휘말렸습니다. 인터넷 뉴스 첫 화면에 그의 사진이 걸렸습니다.
mt: The priest you respected got caught in the scandal, and his picture was on the first screen of the Internet news.
en: A priest you once revered is caught up in a scandal. His photo is splashed across the front page of the online news.

ko: 기도 중 손끝이 따뜻해지는 것을 느낍니다. 전기 스탠드가 깜빡입니다.
mt: I feel my hands warm in my prayers. The electric stand blinks.
en: In prayer, you feel your fingertips grow warm. The desk lamp flickers.

ko: 오래된 경전을 다시 읽다 새로운 의미를 발견했습니다. 책갈피 사이에 낡은 메모가 끼어 있습니다.
mt: I found new meaning in rereading old scriptures. There's an old note in between the bookmarks.
en: Rereading an old scripture, you find new meaning in it. A worn note is tucked between the pages.

ko: 갑작스러운 병으로 며칠간 앓아누웠습니다. 방 안에는 해열제와 한약 냄새가 뒤섞여 있습니다.
mt: I was sick with a sudden illness for a few days, and inside the room there's a mixture of seafood and the smell of a medicine.
en: A sudden illness leaves you bedridden for days. The room smells of fever pills and herbal medicine.

ko: 산속 수도원에서 은둔 수행을 권유받았습니다. 산길에는 안개가 자욱합니다.
mt: I've been invited to cover up in a mountain monastery, and there's a fog on the mountain road.
en: You are invited to a secluded retreat at a mountain monastery. Thick fog hangs over the mountain path.

ko: 당신의 기도가 이루어진 듯한 일이 일어났습니다. 오래 앓던 이웃집 아이가 열이 내렸습니다.
mt: Your old neighbor's child fell out of a fever.
en: Something happens as if your prayer has been answered. The neighbor's long-sick child finally breaks his fever.

ko: 다른 종교의 수행자가 당신에게 논쟁을 청합니다. 그는 시장 한복판에서 확성기를 들고 있습니다.
mt: Another religion's agent invites you to argue, and he's holding a loudspeaker in the middle of the market.
en: A practitioner of another faith challenges you to a debate. He stands in the middle of the market with a megaphone.

ko: 교단 운영에 지쳐 신앙이 메말라 갑니다. 새벽 기도회에 빈자리가 눈에 띕니다.
mt: I'm tired of teaching, and I'm getting tired of believing, and I'm seeing empty seats in the morning prayer.
en: Worn out from running the cult, your faith is running dry. Empty seats stand out at the dawn prayer meeting.

ko: 어린 시절 다니던 교회의 종소리가 문득 그리워집니다. 옛 동네 골목은 이제 아파트 단지가 되었습니다.
mt: I miss the bell of my childhood church, and the old neighborhood alley is now an apartment complex.
en: You suddenly miss the church bells of your childhood. The old neighborhood alleys are apartment blocks now.

ko: 밤하늘의 별똥별을 보며 소원을 빕니다. 옥상 위 빨래가 바람에 펄럭입니다.
mt: I wish I could look at the stars in the night sky, and the clothes on the roof are blowing in the wind.
en: You make a wish on a shooting star. Laundry flaps in the wind on the rooftop.

ko: 측근이 당신의 신앙을 의심하는 말을 엿들었습니다. 복도 끝 문틈으로 목소리가 새어 나옵니다.
mt: I overheard your muscles doubting your faith, and your voice comes out through the door at the end of the hall.
en: You overhear someone in your inner circle doubting your faith. Voices leak through a door ajar at the end of the hall.

ko: 폭풍우 치는 밤 교단 건물에 벼락이 떨어졌습니다. 지붕 한쪽이 불에 그을렸습니다.
mt: On a stormy night, lightning struck the bridge, and one of the roofs caught him in the fire.
en: On a stormy night, lightning strikes the cult's building. One side of the roof is scorched.

ko: 묵상 중 당신의 전생을 본 것 같습니다. 눈을 뜨자 흰 연기가 천장으로 흩어집니다.
mt: I think I've seen your previous life in meditation, and as you open your eyes, white smoke scatters into the ceiling.
en: In meditation, you seem to glimpse a past life. When you open your eyes, white smoke scatters toward the ceiling.

ko: 한 노인이 당신에게 진짜 믿음이 무엇인지 묻습니다. 노인의 손에는 낡은 성경이 들려 있습니다.
mt: An old man asks you what you really believe, and the old man has an old Bible in his hand.
en: An old man asks you what true faith is. He holds a worn Bible in his hands.

ko: 기도문을 새로 지어 보기로 했습니다. 컴퓨터 화면에는 썼다 지운 문장이 가득합니다.
mt: I decided to create a new prayer. The computer screen is full of written sentences.
en: You decide to write a new prayer. Your computer screen is full of sentences written and deleted.

ko: 당신이 신을 잃는 악몽을 꾸었습니다. 깨어 보니 식은땀에 베개가 젖어 있습니다.
mt: You've had a nightmare of losing your God. You wake up and you've got a pillow in your sweat.
en: You have a nightmare in which you lose God. You wake to a pillow soaked in cold sweat.

ko: 한 신도가 가족의 반대로 교단을 떠나려 합니다. 대문 앞에서 가족이 목소리를 높이고 있습니다.
mt: A Shintoist is leaving the church on the other side of the family, and the family is raising their voice in front of the front door.
en: A follower wants to leave the cult because their family objects. The family is raising their voices at the front gate.

ko: 신도들이 집회에서 눈물을 흘리며 찬양합니다. 강당 천장 선풍기가 느리게 돕니다.
mt: The faithful cry and praise at the rally, and the ceiling fan of the hall is slow.
en: Your followers sing praises with tears in their eyes at the gathering. The ceiling fan in the hall turns slowly.

ko: 신도들 사이에 의견 충돌이 생겼습니다. 집회 뒷자리에서 언성이 높아집니다.
mt: There was a conflict between the faithful, and the voices were raised in the back of the rally.
en: A disagreement breaks out among your followers. Voices rise from the back rows of the gathering.

ko: 한 신도가 당신에게 평생 모은 재산을 바치겠다고 합니다. 그의 손에는 낡은 통장이 들려 있습니다.
mt: A Shintoist offers to give you a life-long sum, and in his hand is an old cage.
en: A follower offers you his entire life savings. He holds a battered bankbook.

ko: 신도들이 당신의 생일을 성대하게 축하하려 합니다. 집회소 벽에 색종이가 붙어 있습니다.
mt: I want to congratulate the faithful on your birthday with colored paper on the wall of the rally.
en: Your followers want to throw you a lavish birthday celebration. Colored paper is taped to the walls of the meeting hall.

ko: 어린 신도가 당신을 따라 하며 설교 흉내를 냅니다. 집회소 마룻바닥에서 아이들이 웃음을 터뜨립니다.
mt: A young Shintoist mimics you as a preacher, and the kids laugh at you on the floor of the bar.
en: A young follower imitates you, mimicking your sermons. Children burst into laughter on the meeting hall floor.

ko: 병든 신도가 기적을 바라며 당신을 찾아왔습니다. 그의 얼굴은 창백하고 숨이 가쁩니다.
mt: A sick Shinto came to you, hoping for a miracle, and his face was pale and breathless.
en: A sick follower comes to you hoping for a miracle. His face is pale and his breathing labored.

ko: 한 신도가 꿈에서 당신을 보았다고 간증합니다. 그는 흥분해 목소리가 떨립니다.
mt: A Shintoist may have seen you in a dream, but he's excited and his voice trembles.
en: A follower testifies that he saw you in a dream. His voice trembles with excitement.

ko: 신도들이 교단 생활이 너무 엄격하다고 불평합니다. 식당에서 수군거리는 소리가 들립니다.
mt: The faithful complain that the school life is too strict.
en: Followers complain that cult life is too strict. Whispers drift through the dining hall.

ko: 오래된 신도 한 명이 세상을 떠났습니다. 그의 방에는 낡은 성경과 안경이 놓여 있습니다.
mt: There's an old Shinto who's gone, and there's an old Bible and a pair of glasses in his room.
en: One of your oldest followers has passed away. A worn Bible and a pair of glasses lie in his room.

ko: 신도들이 함께 노래할 찬송가를 원합니다. 피아노 뚜껑 위에 악보가 흩어져 있습니다.
mt: I want a hymn for the believers to sing together, and the music is scattered on the top of the piano.
en: Your followers want a hymn they can sing together. Sheet music is scattered across the piano lid.

ko: 신도 하나가 당신의 사생활에 대한 소문을 퍼뜨렸습니다. 소문은 이미 동네 인터넷 카페 게시판까지 퍼졌습니다.
mt: A Shintoist has spread rumors about your privacy, and rumors have already spread to the local Internet cafe board.
en: A follower has spread rumors about your private life. They have already reached the local online forum.

ko: 신도들이 교단의 상징을 몸에 새기고 싶어 합니다. 문신 가게 간판이 골목에 걸려 있습니다.
mt: The faithful want to have the symbol of the Faith on their bodies, and the tattoo shop sign is hanging in the alley.
en: Your followers want to tattoo the cult's symbol on their bodies. A tattoo parlor sign hangs in the alley.

ko: 새벽 기도회에 나오는 신도가 줄었습니다. 텅 빈 의자들이 어둠 속에 놓여 있습니다.
mt: There's less faith in the morning prayer, and empty chairs are lying in the dark.
en: Fewer followers come to the dawn prayer meeting. Empty chairs sit in the dark.

ko: 신도 부부가 당신에게 아이의 이름을 지어 달라고 합니다. 아기는 포대기 속에서 잠들어 있습니다.
mt: The Shinto couple ask you to name the child, and the baby is asleep in the air.
en: A married couple among your followers asks you to name their child. The baby sleeps swaddled in a blanket.

ko: 신도들 사이에서 당신을 신으로 섬기자는 말이 나옵니다. 집회 중 누군가 큰 소리로 외칩니다.
mt: There's a saying among the believers that we should serve you as a god.
en: Talk spreads among your followers of worshiping you as a god. Someone shouts it aloud during a gathering.

ko: 한 신도가 당신에게 연모의 마음을 고백했습니다. 그녀의 목소리가 떨립니다.
mt: A Shintoist has confessed to you her love-in-law. Her voice trembles.
en: A follower confesses her love for you. Her voice trembles.

ko: 신도들이 단체로 순례를 떠나자고 합니다. 버스 정류장에 신도들이 가득 모여 있습니다.
mt: A group of believers decided to leave for the pilgrimage, and there's a crowd of them at the bus stop.
en: Your followers propose a group pilgrimage. The bus stop is packed with followers.

ko: 신도들이 당신을 위해 밤새 기도해 주었습니다. 아침 햇살이 집회소 창으로 들어옵니다.
mt: The faithful prayed for you all night. The morning sun comes in the window of the rally hall.
en: Your followers prayed for you all night. Morning sunlight streams through the meeting hall windows.

ko: 교단 측근 하나가 운영 방식에 반기를 들었습니다. 회의실 탁자 위에 서류가 흩어져 있습니다.
mt: There's a protest against the way one of the cults operates, and the paperwork is scattered on the table in the conference room.
en: A member of your inner circle rebels against how the cult is run. Papers are strewn across the conference table.

ko: 교단의 위계를 정해야 할 때가 왔습니다. 칠판에는 직분 이름이 빼곡히 적혀 있습니다.
mt: It's time to decide the hierarchy of the hierarchy.
en: The time has come to set the cult's hierarchy. The blackboard is crammed with titles.

ko: 신도들 앞에서 말실수를 했습니다. 강당 안이 잠시 술렁입니다.
mt: I made a mistake in front of the faithful.
en: You misspeak in front of your followers. A murmur ripples through the hall.

ko: 교단을 상징할 의복을 정합니다. 양복점 진열창에 옷감 견본이 가득합니다.
mt: I choose a suit to represent the Faith, and I have a tailor shop window full of material samples.
en: You choose the vestments that will symbolize the cult. The tailor's window is full of fabric swatches.

ko: 신도 하나가 당신의 명령을 어겼습니다. 집회장 뒷문으로 그가 몰래 빠져나갑니다.
mt: One of the Shintoists has broken your command. He sneaks out the back door of the rally.
en: A follower has disobeyed your order. He slips out the back door of the hall.

ko: 교단 집회 장소를 옮길지 고민합니다. 지도 위에 여러 후보지가 표시되어 있습니다.
mt: There's multiple candidates on the map.
en: You consider moving the cult's gathering place. Several candidate sites are marked on the map.

ko: 측근들이 서로 당신의 신임을 얻으려 경쟁합니다. 회식 자리에서도 눈치 싸움이 벌어집니다.
mt: You know, your friends compete for your dignity, and there's a fight that you'll notice in the liturgical table.
en: Your inner circle competes for your favor. Even at dinner, they size each other up.

ko: 당신의 결정에 신도들이 의문을 제기합니다. 집회 중 손을 든 신도가 줄을 잇습니다.
mt: Your decisions are questioned by the faithful, who raise their hands during the rally.
en: Your followers question your decision. During the gathering, hand after hand goes up.

ko: 교단 규칙집을 만들자는 제안이 나왔습니다. 책상에는 낡은 규약집이 펼쳐져 있습니다.
mt: It's suggested that we build a school rule house, and there's an old set of rules on the desk.
en: Someone proposes a rulebook for the cult. An old set of bylaws lies open on the desk.

ko: 다른 교단의 지도자가 동맹을 제안합니다. 찻집 창가 자리에서 그가 웃으며 손을 내밉니다.
mt: The leader of another cult proposes an alliance, and at the window of the teahouse, he opens his hand with a smile.
en: Another cult's leader proposes an alliance. By a teahouse window, he smiles and extends his hand.

ko: 신도들이 당신 앞에 무릎을 꿇기 시작했습니다. 집회장 바닥이 무릎 자국으로 가득합니다.
mt: The faithful have started to kneel before you, the floor is full of knee marks.
en: Your followers have begun to kneel before you. The hall floor is covered with knee marks.

ko: 교단의 문장을 디자인합니다. 인쇄소 책상에는 시안이 여러 장 펼쳐져 있습니다.
mt: I design the sentences of the Faith. There are several pages of design on the printing press desk.
en: You design the cult's emblem. Several drafts are spread across the print shop's desk.

ko: 측근 하나가 교단 자금을 빼돌린 정황이 드러났습니다. 금고 장부의 숫자가 맞지 않습니다.
mt: It turns out that one of the amygdalas has taken the money out of the school, and the number of the vaults is not right.
en: Evidence surfaces that someone in your inner circle has been embezzling cult funds. The numbers in the safe's ledger don't add up.

ko: 중요한 결정을 앞두고 측근 회의가 열렸습니다. 회의실에는 담배 연기가 자욱합니다.
mt: In front of an important decision, a board meeting was held, and the room was full of smoke.
en: Your inner circle meets ahead of a major decision. The conference room is thick with cigarette smoke.

ko: 신도들이 당신에게 직접 결혼 주례를 부탁합니다. 예식장 대신 집회소를 쓰기로 했습니다.
mt: The faithful ask you to marry them themselves, and instead of a wedding ceremony, they're going to use a rally.
en: Your followers ask you to officiate their wedding yourself. They will use the meeting hall instead of a wedding venue.

ko: 교단에 감찰관 직책을 두자는 의견이 나옵니다. 측근들은 서로의 눈치를 살핍니다.
mt: There's an opinion that you should be an inspector at the school, and the members of the church should be aware of each other's perceptions.
en: Someone suggests creating the post of inspector in the cult. Your inner circle eye one another warily.

ko: 신도들이 당신의 말을 받아 적어 책으로 엮자고 합니다. 뒷방에서 복사기가 쉴 새 없이 돌아갑니다.
mt: The faithful take your words, they write them down, they put them together in a book, and the photocopier goes back and forth in the back room.
en: Your followers want to transcribe your words and bind them into a book. In the back room, the copier runs nonstop.

ko: 교단 내 젊은 신도들이 독자적인 모임을 만들었습니다. 모임 안내 전단이 집회소 게시판에 붙어 있습니다.
mt: The young members of the cult have created a private gathering, and the front of the meeting is attached to the convention hall board.
en: The younger followers have formed their own group. A flyer for it is pinned to the meeting hall's notice board.

ko: 당신의 초상화를 집회장에 걸자는 제안이 나왔습니다. 화가가 캔버스 앞에서 붓을 고르고 있습니다.
mt: The artist is picking a brush in front of the canvas.
en: Someone proposes hanging your portrait in the hall. A painter picks out brushes before the canvas.

ko: 헌금함에 익명의 거액이 들어 있었습니다. 봉투에는 이름 대신 빈 칸만 적혀 있습니다.
mt: There was an anonymous amount of money in the contribution box. The envelope had empty columns instead of names.
en: An anonymous large sum turns up in the offering box. The envelope bears only a blank space where a name should be.

ko: 교단 건물 지붕이 새기 시작했습니다. 천장에 누런 얼룩이 번지고 있습니다.
mt: The roof of the bridge is starting to leak, and there's a yellow stain on the ceiling.
en: The cult building's roof has started leaking. A yellow stain spreads across the ceiling.

ko: 한 사업가가 교단에 투자를 제안합니다. 회의실 탁자 위에 계약서가 놓여 있습니다.
mt: A businessman offers to invest in the school board, and there's a contract on the table in the conference room.
en: A businessman offers to invest in the cult. A contract lies on the conference table.

ko: 헌금 액수에 따라 자리를 정하자는 의견이 나왔습니다. 집회소 맨 앞줄 의자가 비어 있습니다.
mt: I've got an opinion that we're going to decide on the amount of money that we're going to make, that the front row of chairs is empty.
en: Someone suggests assigning seats by the size of offerings. The front row of the meeting hall sits empty.

ko: 교단의 상징을 새긴 기념품을 팔아 보자는 제안이 나왔습니다. 상가 가게에 견본이 진열되어 있습니다.
mt: It's suggested that we sell souvenirs with symbols of the Faith, and there's samples in the store.
en: Someone proposes selling souvenirs bearing the cult's symbol. Samples are on display in a shop in the arcade.

ko: 교단 회계를 맡던 신도가 장부에 구멍이 있다고 보고합니다. 장부 귀퉁이에 연필 자국이 보입니다.
mt: The Shintoist who's doing the school accounting reports that there's a hole in the books, and in the corner of the book, we see pencil marks.
en: The follower keeping the cult's accounts reports a hole in the books. Pencil marks show in the ledger's corner.

ko: 가난한 신도가 헌금을 못 내 미안해합니다. 그의 손에는 낡은 장갑이 끼워져 있습니다.
mt: I'm sorry that poor Shinto can't contribute. His hands are covered with old gloves.
en: A poor follower is ashamed he cannot give an offering. He wears tattered gloves.

ko: 교단 이름으로 작은 가게를 열자는 의견이 나왔습니다. 골목에 빈 점포 하나가 나와 있습니다.
mt: There's an opinion that we should open a small store in the name of the Faith, and there's an empty store in the alley.
en: Someone suggests opening a small shop under the cult's name. An empty storefront is up for rent in the alley.

ko: 연말이 되어 교단 재정을 결산합니다. 장부에는 숫자가 빽빽하게 적혀 있습니다.
mt: And at the end of the year, we're setting up a school budget, and the books have a lot of numbers on them.
en: The year is ending, and you close the cult's books. The ledger is packed with figures.

ko: 값비싼 성물을 사자는 제안이 들어왔습니다. 골동품 상인이 상자를 열어 보여 줍니다.
mt: It's suggested that we buy expensive holy things, and the antique merchant opens the box and shows it to us.
en: Someone proposes buying a costly relic. An antique dealer opens a box to show you.

ko: 신도가 도박으로 번 돈을 헌금하려 합니다. 그는 주머니에서 구겨진 지폐 뭉치를 꺼냅니다.
mt: He's going to contribute money earned by gambling, and he's going to take out a bunch of paper money from his pocket.
en: A follower wants to offer money he won gambling. He pulls a wad of crumpled bills from his pocket.

ko: 세무 당국이 교단 재정을 문의해 왔습니다. 세무서 직원이 서류 목록을 펼쳐 듭니다.
mt: The tax authorities have asked for the financial funds of the school, and the tax office staff opens up the paperwork.
en: The tax authorities inquire about the cult's finances. A tax officer unfolds a list of documents.

ko: 신도들이 당신을 위해 새 차를 마련하자고 합니다. 주차장에는 낡은 승합차만 서 있습니다.
mt: They're asking you to set up a new car for them. They're standing in the parking lot in an old car.
en: Your followers want to buy you a new car. Only a battered van sits in the parking lot.

ko: 헌금 바구니가 하나 사라졌습니다. 집회소 뒷문이 열려 있고 바닥에 발자국이 남아 있습니다.
mt: The contribution basket is gone, the back door of the rally is open, and there's footprints on the floor.
en: An offering basket has gone missing. The meeting hall's back door is open, with footprints on the floor.

ko: 교단 소유의 땅을 팔라는 제안이 들어왔습니다. 땅은 읍내 외곽의 풀밭입니다.
mt: It's been suggested that we sell land belonging to the church, and the land is a grass field outside of town.
en: You receive an offer to buy the cult's land. It is a grassy lot on the edge of town.

ko: 신도들이 매달 정기 헌금 제도를 원합니다. 명부 위에 날짜가 가득 적혀 있습니다.
mt: The faithful want to have a regular monthly donation system, and the list is full of dates.
en: Your followers want a monthly offering system. The roster is filled with dates.

ko: 값비싼 연회를 열어 후원자를 모으자는 제안이 나왔습니다. 호텔 연회장에 샹들리에가 빛납니다.
mt: It's suggested that we hold a very expensive banquet and collect sponsors, and there's a chandeliers at the hotel banquet.
en: Someone proposes a lavish banquet to attract patrons. Chandeliers glitter in the hotel ballroom.

ko: 헌금이 갑자기 크게 줄었습니다. 헌금함을 열어 보니 지난달보다 절반도 안 찹니다.
mt: The contribution suddenly dropped significantly, and when I opened the contribution box, it was less than half as much as it was last month.
en: Offerings have suddenly plummeted. The offering box holds less than half of last month's.

ko: 한 재벌가 후손이 신도가 되겠다며 찾아왔습니다. 그의 차는 집회소 앞을 가득 메웁니다.
mt: A bee came to the door, saying he was going to be a believer, and his car filled the front of the rally.
en: The heir of a wealthy conglomerate family comes wanting to join. His cars fill the front of the meeting hall.

ko: 광장에서 즉석 설교를 해 볼 기회가 생겼습니다. 광장 한쪽에서 확성기 소리가 울립니다.
mt: I had the opportunity to give an instant sermon in the square, and the sound of the loudspeaker goes out on one side of the square.
en: You get a chance to preach impromptu in the square. A megaphone blares from one corner of the square.

ko: 한 신도가 친구들을 데려오겠다고 합니다. 그는 주말 계획을 적은 수첩을 보여 줍니다.
mt: A Shintoist says he's going to bring his friends in, and he's going to show them a little notebook on the weekend plan.
en: A follower says he will bring his friends. He shows you a planner with his weekend plans.

ko: 대학가에서 포교를 시도합니다. 캠퍼스 게시판에는 동아리 홍보물과 취업 설명회 포스터가 빼곡합니다.
mt: I'm trying to teach in colleges, and on campus billboards, I've got club promotions and job instruction posters.
en: You try proselytizing in the college district. Campus boards are crammed with club flyers and job fair posters.

ko: 새 신도들이 기존 신도들과 어울리지 못합니다. 식당 한쪽에 두 무리가 따로 앉아 있습니다.
mt: The New Believers don't fit in with the existing ones, two groups sitting separately on one side of the restaurant.
en: New followers aren't mixing with the old ones. Two groups sit apart in the dining hall.

ko: 병원 앞에서 환자 가족들에게 다가갑니다. 대기실 의자마다 지친 얼굴이 앉아 있습니다.
mt: We approach the patient's family in front of the hospital, and every chair in the waiting room has a tired face.
en: You approach patients' families outside a hospital. Every waiting-room chair holds a weary face.

ko: 유명 인사가 교단에 관심을 보입니다. 그의 이름이 신문 연예면에 자주 오르내립니다.
mt: A famous man is interested in the Faith, and his name often goes up and down in newspaper entertainment.
en: A celebrity takes an interest in the cult. His name often appears in the entertainment pages.

ko: 인터넷으로 포교를 해 보자는 의견이 나왔습니다. 젊은 신도가 PC방에서 교단 인터넷 카페를 꾸미고 있습니다.
mt: I was asked to do some teaching on the Internet, and a young Shintoist is building a school Internet cafe in a PC room.
en: Someone suggests proselytizing online. A young follower decorates the cult's web forum from an internet café.

ko: 시골 마을을 순회하며 포교합니다. 논두렁 사이 좁은 길을 낡은 승합차가 덜컹거리며 지납니다.
mt: We go through country villages, and there's a narrow road between the paddocks, where the old carriages hang around.
en: You tour the countryside villages to proselytize. A battered van rattles down a narrow path between rice paddies.

ko: 교도소 수감자들에게 설교할 기회가 생겼습니다. 면회실 철문이 차갑게 닫힙니다.
mt: I have a chance to preach to prison inmates, and the door to the door is shut cold.
en: You get a chance to preach to prison inmates. The visiting room's iron door slams coldly shut.

ko: 신도 수를 부풀려 발표하자는 의견이 나왔습니다. 발표 자료 초안에 숫자가 크게 적혀 있습니다.
mt: It was suggested that the number of members should be raised, and there's a lot of numbers written in the early part of the presentation.
en: Someone suggests inflating the follower count in announcements. The draft presentation shows the number in large print.

ko: 외국인 노동자들이 교단에 관심을 보입니다. 공장 기숙사 앞에 사람들이 모여 있습니다.
mt: Foreign workers are interested in the school, and they're gathered in front of the factory dorm.
en: Migrant workers show interest in the cult. People gather outside the factory dormitory.

ko: 교단을 떠났던 신도가 돌아오고 싶어 합니다. 그는 머뭇거리며 집회소 문 앞에 서 있습니다.
mt: The Shintoist who left the Faith wants to come back. He's standing at the door of the rally.
en: A follower who left the cult wants to return. He hesitates at the meeting hall door.

ko: 경쟁 교단의 신도들이 우리 쪽으로 넘어오려 합니다. 골목 모퉁이에서 두 교단의 신도가 서로 눈치를 봅니다.
mt: The members of the rival cult are trying to get over to us, and on the corner of the alley, the members of the two groups notice each other.
en: Followers of a rival cult want to come over to yours. On a street corner, followers of both cults eye each other.

ko: 축제에서 교단 부스를 운영합니다. 부스 앞에 줄이 길게 늘어서 있습니다.
mt: I run a bridge booth at the festival, and I have a long line in front of it.
en: You run a cult booth at a festival. A long line stretches in front of it.

ko: 한 가족 전체가 입교를 원합니다. 가족은 나란히 서서 당신의 답을 기다립니다.
mt: A whole family wants to go to school, and they stand side by side waiting for your answer.
en: An entire family wants to join. They stand side by side, awaiting your answer.

ko: 노인정에서 포교를 시작합니다. 장기판 소리가 방 안을 가득 채웁니다.
mt: In Noki, we're going to start a possum, and the sound of the chessboard fills the room.
en: You begin proselytizing at a senior center. The clack of janggi pieces fills the room.

ko: 포교 중 길에서 시비가 붙었습니다. 상대는 큰 소리로 교단을 욕합니다.
mt: In the middle of the poaching, I was caught in the street, and my opponent was swearing at the pulpit with a loud voice.
en: While proselytizing, you get into a quarrel on the street. The other man loudly curses the cult.

ko: 교단 소식지를 만들자는 제안이 나왔습니다. 복사기 옆에 종이 다발이 쌓여 있습니다.
mt: We've got a proposal to create a bridge, and there's a bunch of paper on the side of the photocopier.
en: Someone proposes a cult newsletter. Stacks of paper pile up beside the copier.

ko: 청년 신도들이 동네 아이들에게 무료 과외를 하자고 합니다. 교회 마당에 아이들이 모여듭니다.
mt: The young men ask the local kids to give free tutorials, and they gather in the church yard.
en: Young followers want to tutor neighborhood kids for free. Children gather in the churchyard.

ko: 교리의 첫 번째 계율을 정합니다. 낡은 공책에 계율 후보들이 적혀 있습니다.
mt: I set the first rule of doctrine, the first rule of the doctrine, and in an old notebook, there's the rule candidates.
en: You set the first commandment of your Doctrine. Candidate commandments fill an old notebook.

ko: 교리에 금식일을 넣을지 고민합니다. 달력 위에 빈 칸이 가득합니다.
mt: Whether to put a fast day into the doctrine, the calendar is full of empty columns.
en: You consider adding fast days to the Doctrine. The calendar is full of empty squares.

ko: 신도 하나가 교리의 모순을 지적했습니다. 그는 교리 공책을 펼쳐 들고 있습니다.
mt: One of the Shintoists pointed out the contradiction of doctrine, and he's holding up the doctrine.
en: A follower points out a contradiction in the Doctrine. He holds the Doctrine notebook open.

ko: 사후 세계에 대한 교리를 정리합니다. 빛바랜 불경 책이 책상에 놓여 있습니다.
mt: It's a book on the desk.
en: You set down the Doctrine on the afterlife. A faded Buddhist sutra lies on the desk.

ko: 성관계에 대한 교리를 정해야 합니다. 회의실 문틈으로 긴 토론 소리가 새어 나옵니다.
mt: You have to have a doctrine about sex, and you have to have a long discussion coming out of the door of the conference room.
en: You must set the Doctrine on sex. Long debate leaks through the conference room door.

ko: 재물에 대한 교리를 정합니다. 시장 노점에서 흥정하는 소리가 들려옵니다.
mt: I hear a bargain at the market stand.
en: You set the Doctrine on wealth. Haggling echoes from the market stalls.

ko: 교리를 정리한 경전 초안이 완성되었습니다. 출력한 원고 뭉치가 책상 위에 쌓여 있습니다.
mt: The canon is complete with the summation of the doctrine, and it has a bunch of printed manuscripts on its desk.
en: A draft scripture codifying the Doctrine is complete. A stack of printed manuscript sits on the desk.

ko: 다른 종교의 교리를 일부 차용할지 고민합니다. 서가에는 여러 종교 서적이 나란히 꽂혀 있습니다.
mt: I'm trying to figure out if I'm going to take some of the doctrines of other religions, and there's a lot of religious literature in the library.
en: You consider borrowing parts of other religions' doctrines. Books on many faiths stand side by side on the shelf.

ko: 교리에 매일의 기도 횟수를 정합니다. 벽시계가 똑딱거리고 있습니다.
mt: I'm defining the number of daily prayers to doctrine, and I've got my panel clock ticking.
en: You set the number of daily prayers in the Doctrine. The wall clock ticks.

ko: 신도들이 교리 공부 모임을 원합니다. 교회 지하 강의실에 의자가 줄지어 놓여 있습니다.
mt: The faithful want to study the doctrine, and there's a row of chairs in the basement of the church.
en: Your followers want a Doctrine study group. Chairs are lined up in the church basement classroom.

ko: 종말에 대한 교리를 넣자는 의견이 나왔습니다. 텔레비전에서 종말 예언을 다룬 특집 방송이 나옵니다.
mt: We've come up with an idea for the doctrine of the end of the world: a special television broadcast of the apocalypse.
en: Someone suggests adding an end-times Doctrine. A TV special on doomsday prophecies is airing.

ko: 교리에 음식 금기를 정합니다. 식당 메뉴판이 교리 공책 옆에 펼쳐져 있습니다.
mt: The restaurant menu is spread beside the dogma.
en: You set dietary taboos in the Doctrine. A restaurant menu lies open beside the Doctrine notebook.

ko: 교리의 상징 동물을 정합니다. 동물도감이 펼쳐져 있습니다.
mt: The animal is also a symbol of doctrine.
en: You choose the Doctrine's sacred animal. An animal encyclopedia lies open.

ko: 교리 해석을 두고 측근들이 두 파로 갈렸습니다. 회의실 문 앞에 두 무리가 서 있습니다.
mt: There are two groups standing at the door of the conference room.
en: Your inner circle splits into two factions over interpreting the Doctrine. Two groups stand outside the conference room.

ko: 교리에 고행 의식을 넣을지 고민합니다. 산 속 기도원의 바위길이 떠오릅니다.
mt: I'm trying to figure out if I'm going to put a high ritual in a doctrine, and I'm going to come up with a rock in a mountain prayer hall.
en: You consider adding rites of mortification to the Doctrine. You picture the rocky path to a mountain prayer house.

ko: 교리에 명절을 만듭니다. 달력에 붉은 표시를 할 날짜를 고릅니다.
mt: This creates a holiday for the doctrine, and we'll pick a date to red on the calendar.
en: You create holy days for the Doctrine. You pick dates to mark in red on the calendar.

ko: 교리를 아이들도 이해할 수 있게 쉽게 쓰자는 의견이 나옵니다. 교육관 벽에 그림이 걸려 있습니다.
mt: It's an idea to make doctrine easy for children to understand, and it's on the walls of the school hall.
en: Someone suggests rewriting the Doctrine so even children can understand it. Drawings hang on the education hall walls.

ko: 교리 속 죄와 벌을 정합니다. 교무실 칠판에 죄목이 적혀 있습니다.
mt: There's a charge on the blackboard of the schoolroom.
en: You define sin and punishment in the Doctrine. A list of offenses is written on the staff room blackboard.

ko: 오래된 교리 하나가 시대에 맞지 않는다는 지적이 나왔습니다. 텔레비전 뉴스가 교리 조항을 비판합니다.
mt: One old doctrine has been pointed out that it doesn't fit into the age, and television news criticizes the dogma.
en: Someone argues an old tenet no longer fits the times. A TV news report criticizes the clause.

ko: 기도 중 누군가 귓가에 속삭이는 소리가 들립니다. 방 안에는 당신뿐입니다.
mt: In the middle of the prayer, you hear someone whispering in your ear, you're the only one in the room.
en: While praying, you hear someone whisper in your ear. You are alone in the room.

ko: 교단 건물 지하에서 오래된 제단을 발견했습니다. 제단에는 그을린 촛농이 굳어 있습니다.
mt: We found an old altar in the basement of the bridge, and on the altar there's a hard wax.
en: You discover an old altar in the cult building's basement. Scorched wax has hardened upon it.

ko: 명상 중 몸이 공중에 뜨는 듯한 감각을 느꼈습니다. 깨어 보니 방석 위에 앉아 있습니다.
mt: I felt as if my body were in the air during meditation, and when I woke up, I was sitting on a cushion.
en: In meditation, you feel as if your body is floating. When you come to, you are sitting on your cushion.

ko: 한 신도가 당신에게서 빛이 났다고 증언합니다. 그는 떨리는 목소리로 말합니다.
mt: A Shintoist has testified to the light from you, and he says in a trembling voice,
en: A follower testifies that light shone from you. He speaks in a trembling voice.

ko: 오래된 무당이 당신을 찾아와 접신의 비법을 알려 주겠다고 합니다. 그녀의 옷자락에서 향 냄새가 납니다.
mt: An old shaman will come to you and tell you the secret of the reception, and it smells like incense in her skirt.
en: An old shaman visits, offering to teach you the secrets of Communion. Her robes smell of incense.

ko: 깊은 밤 촛불이 저절로 꺼졌습니다. 창문은 닫혀 있고 바람도 없습니다.
mt: Deep in the night, the candle was turned off by itself. The windows were closed and there was no wind.
en: Deep in the night, a candle goes out on its own. The window is shut, and there is no wind.

ko: 신도들과 함께 황홀경에 빠지는 의식을 엽니다. 다락방에 북과 향로가 놓여 있습니다.
mt: There's an infatuation with the faithful, and in the attic, there's a north and a furnace.
en: You hold an ecstatic rite with your followers. Drums and a censer sit in the attic.

ko: 예언처럼 들리는 말이 당신 입에서 흘러나왔습니다. 본인도 무슨 뜻인지 모릅니다.
mt: The prophetic word came out of your mouth, and you don't know what it means.
en: Words like prophecy spill from your mouth. Even you don't know what they mean.

ko: 오래 비어 있던 성소에 들어가 하룻밤을 보냅니다. 먼지가 쌓인 제대 위에 촛대가 하나 있습니다.
mt: They go into the old empty sanctuary overnight, and there's a candlestick on top of a pile of dust.
en: You spend a night in a long-abandoned sanctuary. A single candlestick stands on the dusty altar.

ko: 동물들이 당신 주위에 모여드는 일이 잦아졌습니다. 마당의 참새와 고양이가 가까이 옵니다.
mt: It's become more frequent that animals gather around you, and the sparrows and the cats in the yard come close.
en: Animals gather around you more and more often. Sparrows and cats in the yard come close.

ko: 꿈속에서 거대한 뱀이 당신에게 이름을 묻습니다. 뱀의 눈은 금빛입니다.
mt: In a dream, a giant snake asks you its name. The snake's eyes are golden.
en: In a dream, a giant serpent asks your name. Its eyes are golden.

ko: 교단의 성물이 미세하게 떨리는 것을 발견했습니다. 제단 위 향로 뚜껑이 덜컹거립니다.
mt: We found that the church's sacred substance was shaking in a fine way, and the top of the altar was a little bit of a smudge.
en: You notice the cult's relic trembling faintly. The censer lid on the altar rattles.

ko: 오랫동안 아팠던 신도가 당신의 기도 후 회복했습니다. 그는 병원 진단서를 들고 찾아왔습니다.
mt: A long, sick Shintoist recovered after praying to you, and he came with a medical certificate.
en: A follower who was ill for years recovers after your prayer. He comes to you holding a hospital report.

ko: 접신 중 낯선 존재가 대가를 요구합니다. 목소리는 차갑고 또렷합니다.
mt: A strange presence demands payment, and the voice is cold and clear.
en: During Communion, a strange presence demands a price. Its voice is cold and clear.

ko: 교단 근처 우물에서 이상한 빛이 올라옵니다. 우물가 돌에 이끼가 가득합니다.
mt: A strange light comes up from a well near the bridge, and it's filled with moss.
en: A strange light rises from a well near the cult. The stones around it are thick with moss.

ko: 신도 하나가 접신 체험을 했다고 주장합니다. 그는 흥분해서 손을 떨고 있습니다.
mt: One of the Shintoists claims he's had a close-up experience, and he's shaking his hand with excitement.
en: A follower claims to have experienced Communion. He is so excited his hands shake.

ko: 일식이 일어나는 날입니다. 하늘이 어두워지고 새들이 울음을 그칩니다.
mt: It's the day the eclipse takes place, the sky gets dark and the birds stop crying.
en: It is the day of a solar eclipse. The sky darkens, and the birds fall silent.

ko: 오래된 무덤가에서 기도하자 바람이 멎었습니다. 풀숲에서 벌레 소리가 뚝 끊깁니다.
mt: When we prayed at the old graveside, the wind stopped, and in the grass, the insects stopped ringing.
en: When you pray by an old grave, the wind dies. The insects in the grass go suddenly quiet.

ko: 지역 신문이 교단을 취재하고 싶어 합니다. 편집국 기자가 명함을 내밉니다.
mt: The local newspaper wants to cover the school.
en: The local paper wants to cover the cult. A reporter from the newsroom holds out a business card.

ko: 교단에 대한 악성 루머가 퍼지고 있습니다. 동네 미용실과 인터넷 카페마다 그 얘기가 오갑니다.
mt: There's a vicious rumor going on about cults, and every beauty neighborhood and every Internet cafe is talking about it.
en: Malicious rumors about the cult are spreading. They are the talk of every local salon and online forum.

ko: 재해 이재민을 돕자는 요청이 들어왔습니다. 텔레비전에서 물에 잠긴 마을이 나옵니다.
mt: We've been asked to help victims of disaster, and we've got a village in the water on television.
en: You are asked to help disaster victims. The TV shows a village underwater.

ko: 동네 주민들이 교단의 소음에 항의합니다. 야심한 시간까지 이어지는 기도 소리가 문제입니다.
mt: Locals protest to the noise of the cults, and the prayer that goes on to the harsh times is a problem.
en: Locals complain about the noise from the cult. Prayers that run late into the night are the problem.

ko: 시장 선거 후보가 교단의 지지를 원합니다. 후보의 선거 차량이 교단 앞을 지나갑니다.
mt: The mayor's election candidate wants to be supported by the Faith, and the candidate's election car is going to be in front of it.
en: A mayoral candidate wants the cult's endorsement. His campaign truck rolls past the cult's door.

ko: 교단 신도가 범죄를 저질러 뉴스에 나왔습니다. 텔레비전 뉴스 화면에 교단 건물이 잠깐 비칩니다.
mt: A cult member is on the news for a crime, and it's just a short time on the television news screen.
en: A follower commits a crime and makes the news. The cult building flashes briefly on the TV screen.

ko: 무료 급식소를 열자는 제안이 나왔습니다. 빈 공터에 취사 도구가 쌓여 있습니다.
mt: It's suggested that we open a free kitchen, and there's a stack of service tools in the open.
en: Someone proposes opening a free soup kitchen. Cooking gear is piled in an empty lot.

ko: 교단을 비판하는 책이 출간되었습니다. 서점 진열대 맨 앞에 그 책이 놓여 있습니다.
mt: A book was published that criticized the hierarchy, and it was at the top of the bookstore.
en: A book criticizing the cult is published. It sits at the front of the bookstore display.

ko: 지역 축제의 후원을 요청받았습니다. 축제 현수막이 마을 입구에 걸려 있습니다.
mt: The fiesta is hanging at the entrance of the village.
en: You are asked to sponsor a local festival. A festival banner hangs at the village entrance.

ko: 교단 출신 유명인이 교단을 비난했습니다. 그의 인터뷰가 텔레비전 시사 프로그램에 나옵니다.
mt: A famous catechist criticized the Faith, and his interview appeared on a television news program.
en: A celebrity ex-member denounces the cult. His interview airs on a TV current-affairs show.

ko: 방송국에서 사이비 종교 특집에 교단을 다루려 합니다. 방송국 카메라가 교단 앞마당에 세워져 있습니다.
mt: The station's going to run a cult on a cult speciality, and it's set up in the front yard.
en: A broadcaster wants to feature the cult in a special on pseudo-religions. A TV camera stands in the cult's front yard.

ko: 동네 청소 봉사에 교단이 참여합니다. 골목마다 쓰레기봉투가 쌓여 있습니다.
mt: A group joins in the community cleaning service, and there's a pile of garbage bags in every alley.
en: The cult joins a neighborhood cleanup. Garbage bags pile up in every alley.

ko: 종교 지도자 모임에 초대받았습니다. 회관 로비에서 명패가 나란히 놓여 있습니다.
mt: I've been invited to a religious leadership group, and there's a lot of business going on in the lobby of the hall.
en: You are invited to a gathering of religious leaders. Nameplates stand side by side in the hall lobby.

ko: 교단이 운영하는 쉼터에 기부가 쏟아집니다. 쉼터 게시판에 기부자 이름이 빼곡히 적혀 있습니다.
mt: Donations are poured into the shelters run by the church, and on the shelter board, the donor's name is inscribed.
en: Donations pour into the shelter the cult runs. The shelter's board is crammed with donors' names.

ko: 인근 학교에서 교단 신도 학생이 따돌림을 당한다고 합니다. 교문 앞에서 학부모들이 웅성댑니다.
mt: At a nearby school, a student of the faith is being left out, and the parents are shouting in front of the door.
en: A student follower is reportedly being bullied at a nearby school. Parents murmur outside the school gate.

ko: 명망 있는 학자가 교단을 연구하겠다고 합니다. 그는 노트를 펼쳐 놓고 질문 목록을 적고 있습니다.
mt: A respected scholar says he's going to study the Faith, he's going to put out his notes, he's going to write down a list of questions.
en: A renowned scholar wants to study the cult. He has a notebook open and is writing a list of questions.

ko: 교단 이름으로 장학금을 주자는 제안이 나왔습니다. 장학금 신청서 양식이 책상 위에 놓여 있습니다.
mt: It's suggested that we give scholarships by the name of the Faith, and the form of applications for scholarships is on the desk.
en: Someone proposes a scholarship in the cult's name. Application forms lie on the desk.

ko: 이웃 교회 목사가 교단에 화해의 손길을 내밉니다. 그는 찻잔을 든 채 기다리고 있습니다.
mt: A neighboring church minister extends the hand of reconciliation to the church. He's waiting for a cup of tea.
en: The pastor of a neighboring church extends an olive branch to the cult. He waits, teacup in hand.

ko: 신도가 스무 명을 넘었습니다. 교단이 제법 모양을 갖춥니다.
mt: The faithful have more than 20 members, and the Faith has its own shape.
en: You now have more than twenty followers. The cult is starting to take shape.

ko: 신도가 쉰 명을 넘었습니다. 집회 장소가 비좁아졌습니다.
mt: The congregation is over 50 people. The meeting place is cramped.
en: You now have more than fifty followers. The gathering place has grown cramped.

ko: 신도가 백 명을 넘었습니다. 언론이 교단을 주목하기 시작합니다.
mt: There are over a hundred members. The press is starting to look at the cults.
en: You now have more than a hundred followers. The press begins to take notice of the cult.

ko: 신도가 이백 명을 넘었습니다. 지부를 세우자는 목소리가 높습니다.
mt: There are over two hundred members, and there are high voices to set up the branch.
en: You now have more than two hundred followers. Voices grow louder calling for a branch.

ko: 신도들의 믿음이 깊어져 자발적인 간증이 이어집니다.
mt: The faith of the faithful is deeply rooted, and it leads to spontaneous liverism.
en: Your followers' faith deepens, and testimonies pour forth unprompted.

ko: 신도들이 당신을 위해서라면 무엇이든 하겠다고 맹세합니다. 집회소 안이 뜨거운 열기로 가득합니다.
mt: The faithful will do anything for you. The rally is full of hot heat.
en: Your followers swear they would do anything for you. The meeting hall burns with fervor.

ko: 신도들의 믿음이 광신에 가까워졌습니다. 외부의 시선이 따갑습니다.
mt: The faith of the faithful has drawn us closer to fanaticism. It's a bit of an outside view.
en: Your followers' faith borders on fanaticism. Outsiders' stares are sharp.

mt: The Faith's vault is well stocked.
en: The cult's coffers are flush.

ko: 막대한 헌금이 쌓이자 이를 노리는 자들이 나타났습니다. 금고 주변에서 낯선 사내들이 서성입니다.
mt: There's a huge stack of contributions, and there's a bunch of strangers around the vault.
en: As offerings pile up, those who covet them appear. Strange men loiter near the safe.

mt: The Faith vault is out. The faithful are nervous.
en: The cult's coffers are empty. Your followers grow uneasy.

ko: 측근들이 당신의 눈치를 보며 아무도 반대하지 않습니다.
mt: The amygdalas look at your notice and no one's against you.
en: Your inner circle watches your mood, and no one objects anymore.

mt: Your words soon became law.
en: Your word has become law.

ko: 당신의 신앙이 한층 깊어졌습니다. 기도가 더 이상 말이 아닌 대화처럼 느껴집니다.
mt: Your faith has grown deeper. Your prayers no longer seem like words, but like conversations.
en: Your faith has deepened. Prayer no longer feels like words, but like conversation.

ko: 신이 당신에게 직접 모습을 드러낸 것 같습니다. 빛이 방 안을 가득 채우다 사라집니다.
mt: God appears to have revealed himself to you. Light fills the room and disappears.
en: God seems to have revealed Himself to you. Light fills the room, then vanishes.

ko: 접신이 깊어지며 꿈과 현실의 경계가 흐려집니다.
mt: The communication deepens, and the boundaries between dreams and reality become blurry.
en: As your Communion deepens, the line between dream and reality blurs.

ko: 당신의 말에 이상한 힘이 깃들기 시작했습니다.
mt: You're starting to have strange power in your words.
en: A strange power begins to dwell in your words.

ko: 완전한 접신에 이르렀습니다. 당신은 신의 목소리 그 자체가 되었습니다.
mt: You became the voice of God itself.
en: You have reached perfect Communion. You have become the very voice of God.

mt: Doctrine began to have a system.
en: Your Doctrine begins to take systematic form.

ko: 교리를 둘러싼 이단 논쟁이 일어났습니다. 신학 잡지에 공방이 실립니다.
mt: There's an argument around doctrine, and there's a debate in the theology magazine.
en: A heresy dispute erupts over your Doctrine. Theological journals print the back-and-forth.

ko: 교리가 완성에 가까워지자 교단 밖에서도 연구 대상이 되었습니다. 대학 연구실에서 교리 번역본을 펼쳐 봅니다.
mt: And as the doctrine got closer to completion, it became a subject for research outside the church, and it opened up a translation of the doctrine in the university's lab.
en: As your Doctrine nears completion, it becomes an object of study beyond the cult. In a university lab, someone opens a translation of it.

ko: 교단의 평판이 크게 떨어졌습니다. 거리에서 신도들이 손가락질을 받습니다.
mt: The church's reputation has fallen dramatically, and members of the congregation get fingered in the streets.
en: The cult's Repute has plummeted. Followers are pointed at in the street.

ko: 교단이 사회적 지탄의 대상이 되었습니다. 당국의 조사가 시작됩니다.
mt: The Faith became the target of social criticism. The authorities began to investigate.
en: The cult has become a target of public condemnation. The authorities open an investigation.

ko: 교단이 지역 사회에서 존경받는 단체가 되었습니다.
mt: The Faith became a respected group in the community.
en: The cult has become a respected organization in the community.

ko: 신도는 많지만 믿음이 얕습니다. 교단이 흔들립니다.
mt: There's a lot of faithful, but the faith is shallow. The cults are shaken.
en: Your followers are many, but their faith is shallow. The cult is wavering.

ko: 돈은 넘치지만 평판은 바닥입니다. 사람들은 교단을 돈벌이 집단이라 부릅니다.
mt: It's a lot of money, but it's a disrepute, and people call it a money group.
en: Money overflows, but Repute is at rock bottom. People call the cult a money-making racket.

ko: 권위는 높지만 신도들의 마음이 떠나고 있습니다.
mt: Authority is high, but the hearts of the faithful are gone.
en: Your Authority is high, but your followers' hearts are drifting away.

ko: 신도는 늘었지만 정작 당신의 신앙은 바닥입니다.
mt: Your faith is dead.
en: Your followers have grown in number, yet your own faith is at rock bottom.

ko: 교단이 세력을 이루자 다른 교단들이 견제하기 시작했습니다.
mt: As the cults gained power, other cults began to take over.
en: As the cult gains power, other cults begin to keep it in check.

ko: 접신 체험이 교리와 맞물리며 새로운 계시가 내려옵니다.
mt: A new revelation comes from an experience that meets the doctrine.
en: Your Communion experiences dovetail with the Doctrine, and a new Revelation descends.

ko: 교주와 신도의 믿음이 하나로 맞물렸습니다. 교단에 성스러운 기운이 감돕니다.
mt: The faith of the teacher and the Shintoist is united, and the sacred spirit of the church is lifted up.
en: The faith of leader and followers has become one. A holy aura hangs over the cult.

ko: 동네 주민들이 교단 건물 앞에서 반대 시위를 벌입니다. 피켓이 담벼락에 줄지어 서 있습니다.
mt: Local residents protest in front of the church building, and there's a line of picketts on the wall.
en: Locals stage a protest outside the cult's building. Picket signs line the wall.

ko: 지역의 여러 종교 단체가 연합해 교단을 이단으로 규정했습니다.
mt: A number of local religious groups have united to define the cult as a branch.
en: Religious groups across the region have united to brand the cult heretical.

ko: 국가 기관이 교단에 대한 공식 조사에 착수했습니다. 관공서 직원들이 서류 상자를 옮기고 있습니다.
mt: The government has launched a formal investigation into the school, and the officials are moving the papers.
en: A state agency has launched an official investigation into the cult. Officials are carrying out boxes of documents.

ko: 정부가 교단 해체 명령을 검토하고 있다는 소식입니다. 시간이 많지 않습니다.
mt: We don't have a lot of time.
en: Word is the government is considering an order to dissolve the cult. Time is short.

ko: 지역 단체들이 교단에 공동 사업을 제안해 왔습니다.
mt: Local organizations have proposed a co-communication.
en: Local organizations propose joint projects with the cult.

ko: 정부에서 교단을 정식 종교 법인으로 인정하는 절차를 안내해 왔습니다.
mt: I've been leading a process in which the government recognizes the Church as a formal religious corporation.
en: The government has sent guidance on recognizing the cult as an official religious corporation.

ko: 교단이 지역 사회의 상징이 되었습니다. 언론이 교주의 인터뷰를 요청합니다.
mt: The press is asking for a sympathetic interview.
en: The cult has become a symbol of the community. The press requests an interview with the cult leader.

ko: 신도들의 가족이 교단을 고소하겠다며 모였습니다. 교단 앞에서 가족들이 피켓을 들고 있습니다.
mt: The family of the faithful are gathered to sue the Faith, and in front of it, they're holding a picket.
en: Followers' families gather, threatening to sue the cult. They hold picket signs outside the cult.

ko: 기도를 올려도 아무 응답이 없습니다. 몇 달째 신의 목소리는 끊겼고, 새벽마다 빈 방에 홀로 앉아 있습니다.
mt: For months, God's voice has been broken, and he sits alone in an empty room every morning.
en: You pray, but there is no answer. God's voice has been silent for months, and every dawn you sit alone in an empty room.

ko: 설교 도중 갑자기 말문이 막혔습니다. 수십 개의 눈이 당신을 향해 있고, 어디까지 말했는지 떠오르지 않습니다.
mt: And all of a sudden, in the middle of the sermon, I was stuck, and I couldn't remember how many dozens of eyes were pointing at you, and how far they were talking.
en: Mid-sermon, the words suddenly fail you. Dozens of eyes are on you, and you can't recall where you left off.

ko: 집회에서 신도들이 기계적으로 입만 움직입니다. 눈빛에는 믿음이 없고 시계만 힐끔거립니다.
mt: At the rally, the believers move their mouths mechanically, they have no faith in the eyes, they have no watch.
en: At the gathering, your followers mouth the words mechanically. There is no faith in their eyes; they keep glancing at the clock.

ko: 고참 신도 하나가 집회에서 공개적으로 교단을 떠나겠다고 선언했습니다. 그의 목소리가 강당에 울립니다.
mt: One of the veterans announced in a rally that he was going to leave the church publicly, and his voice rang in the auditorium.
en: A veteran follower publicly announces at the gathering that he is leaving the cult. His voice rings through the hall.

ko: 측근 하나가 당신의 명령을 대놓고 무시하고 자기 모임을 꾸렸습니다. 그 모임에 신도들이 하나둘 드나듭니다.
mt: One of the aides ignored your orders and set up a meeting of their own, where a group of believers will come and go.
en: Someone in your inner circle openly ignores your orders and forms his own group. One by one, followers drift in and out of it.

ko: 한 신도가 집회에서 일어나 교주 자리가 자신의 몫이라고 외칩니다. 몇몇은 박수를 보냅니다.
mt: A Shintoist stands up at a rally shouting that the teacher's seat is his share, and some people applaud.
en: A follower rises at the gathering and shouts that the leader's seat is rightfully his. A few applaud.

ko: 집회소 주인이 밀린 월세를 받으러 문을 두드립니다. 이번 달 안에 못 내면 건물을 비우라고 합니다.
mt: The owner knocks on the door to receive a push-by rent, and if you can't get out in this month, we'll have the building empty.
en: The meeting hall's owner knocks to collect overdue rent. Pay by the end of the month, he says, or vacate.

ko: 한겨울 난방비가 끊겨 집회소에 연탄도 못 땝니다. 신도들이 외투를 껴입고 떨고 있습니다.
mt: There's no heating costs in the middle of the winter, and there's no fuel in the shelter, and the faithful are wearing their coats and trembling.
en: The heating money has run out in the dead of winter; there isn't even coal for the hall. Followers shiver in layered coats.

ko: 새벽 집회 시간, 문을 열었지만 아무도 오지 않았습니다. 빈 의자가 어둠 속에 늘어서 있습니다.
mt: At the time of the meeting in the morning, we opened the door, but no one came, and there's an empty chair in the dark.
en: At the hour of the dawn gathering, you open the doors, but no one comes. Empty chairs stand in rows in the dark.

ko: 마지막까지 남아 있던 신도가 이사를 가게 되었다며 작별 인사를 건넵니다. 그는 미안한 얼굴로 서 있습니다.
mt: He says goodbye to the last Shintoist who's been left to move, and he's standing with a sorry face.
en: Your last remaining follower comes to say goodbye; he is moving away. He stands there, apologetic.

ko: 한 청년이 교리가 무엇이냐고 따져 묻는데 마땅히 대답할 말이 없습니다. 정리된 교리 문장 하나 없는 것이 드러났습니다.
mt: It turns out there's not a single set of dogmas.
en: A young man demands to know what your Doctrine is, and you have no good answer. It's clear you have not a single coherent tenet.

ko: 낡은 필사본 교리 노트가 비에 젖어 번졌습니다. 오랜 밤 적어 둔 문장 절반이 알아볼 수 없게 되었습니다.
mt: The old manuscript doctrinal notes were spread in the rain, and half of the sentences that were written in the long night were unrecognizable.
en: Your old handwritten Doctrine notebook is soaked and smeared by rain. Half the sentences from many long nights are illegible.

ko: 접신 의식 중 아무것도 느껴지지 않습니다. 향이 다 타도록 눈을 감고 있었지만 어둠뿐입니다.
mt: I don't feel anything in the receiving ceremony, and I'm closing my eyes to burn all the incense, but only the darkness.
en: You feel nothing during the Communion rite. You keep your eyes closed until the incense burns out, but there is only darkness.

ko: 접신을 시도하던 밤, 어둠 속에서 알 수 없는 공허한 울림이 들렸습니다. 눈을 뜨니 촛불이 모두 꺼져 있습니다.
mt: And on the night of the reception, I heard an unknown hollow sound in the dark, and I opened my eyes, and the candles were all turned off.
en: On a night you attempt Communion, a hollow, unknowable resonance sounds in the dark. When you open your eyes, every candle is out.

ko: 교단 건물 담벼락에 사이비라는 낙서가 붙었습니다. 지나가는 사람들이 혀를 차며 수군거립니다.
mt: There's a graffiti called Cybi on the walls of a bridge building, and the people who are passing are kicking their tongues.
en: Someone has scrawled "pseudo-religion" on the cult building's wall. Passersby click their tongues and whisper.

ko: 이웃 주민이 교단이 수상하다며 파출소에 신고했습니다. 경찰이 찾아와 신분증 제시를 요구합니다.
mt: A neighbor called the police and demanded an ID.
en: A neighbor reports the cult to the police box as suspicious. An officer comes and demands your ID.

ko: 신도들이 바친 헌금으로 성대한 만찬을 엽니다. 손님들이 당신을 우러러봅니다.
mt: You have a big dinner with the faithful's contributions, and the guests look up to you.
en: You hold a lavish banquet with your followers' offerings. The guests look up to you.

ko: 황금 제단을 짓자는 제안이 들어옵니다. 신도들은 기꺼이 손을 모읍니다.
mt: A proposal is made to build a golden altar, and the believers are willing to raise their hands.
en: Someone proposes building a golden altar. Your followers gladly pool their hands.

ko: 명품 정장이 기부로 들어왔습니다. 입어 보니 누구도 감히 말을 걸지 못합니다.
mt: A luxury suit came in as a donation, and when you put it on, no one dares talk.
en: A designer suit arrives as a donation. When you put it on, no one dares speak to you.

ko: 지역 유지가 교단 후원을 약속합니다. 대가는 작은 자리 하나입니다.
mt: Local is promised support by the school. The price is one small position.
en: A local bigwig pledges to sponsor the cult. The price is one small seat.

ko: 교단 수련원 정원에 분수가 완공되었습니다. 사람들이 몰려와 물가에서 기도합니다.
mt: A fountain has been completed in the school's teaching staff's garden, and people come and pray at the waterfront.
en: The fountain in the retreat's garden is complete. People flock to pray at the water's edge.

ko: 사치스러운 연회 소식이 소문으로 퍼집니다. 궁금해하는 이들이 줄을 섭니다.
mt: The news of a lavish banquet is spread by rumors, and the people who are curious are in line.
en: Rumors of your extravagant banquets spread. The curious line up.

ko: 교단 소유의 땅이 신도시 개발 지역에 들어갔습니다. 땅값이 하룻밤 새 몇 배로 뛰었습니다.
mt: The church-owned land entered the new city development area, and the price of land jumped several times a night.
en: The cult's land falls within a new-town development zone. Its value multiplies overnight.

ko: 당신의 초상화가 새 성전 벽에 걸립니다. 사람들은 그 앞에서 무릎을 꿇습니다.
mt: Your portrait falls on the new temple wall. People kneel before it.
en: Your portrait is hung on the new temple's wall. People kneel before it.

ko: 재벌가 사모님이 교단에 큰 보석을 바칩니다.
mt: His wife offers a large gem to the church.
en: The wife of a chaebol family offers the cult a large jewel.

ko: 군중이 당신의 이름을 연호합니다. 황홀한 기분이 온몸을 감쌉니다.
mt: The crowd is bearing your name, and the feeling of ecstasy fills your whole body.
en: The crowd chants your name. Ecstasy washes over your whole body.

ko: 국회의원이 교단 행사를 후원하겠다며 보좌관을 보냅니다.
mt: A member of Congress sends an aide to sponsor a school event.
en: A member of parliament sends an aide, offering to sponsor a cult event.

ko: 값비싼 침향이 제단에 쌓였습니다. 향내가 골목 끝까지 퍼집니다.
mt: An expensiveloid has been piled up on the altar, and the smell spreads to the edge of the alley.
en: Costly agarwood piles up on the altar. Its scent reaches the end of the alley.

ko: 교단 성전의 종이 새로 주조되었습니다. 종소리에 맞춰 신도들이 몰려듭니다.
mt: The bridge's bell has been composed, and the faithful flock to the sound of the bell.
en: A new bell is cast for the cult's temple. At its toll, followers come flocking.

ko: 검은 외제 승용차가 교단 앞에 멈춥니다. 차에서 내린 사업가는 누구보다 많은 기부금을 약속합니다.
mt: A black car stops in front of the church, and the business people in the car promise to give more money than anyone else.
en: A black imported sedan stops outside the cult. The businessman who steps out pledges a bigger donation than anyone.

ko: 인기 가수가 교단 공연에 오고 싶다고 합니다. 공연장이 가득 찹니다.
mt: A popular singer wants to come to a school performance, and there's a lot of theaters.
en: A popular singer wants to perform at a cult concert. The venue is packed.

ko: 여러 교단이 당신에게 합병을 제안합니다. 거절하면 아쉬운 소리를 듣겠지요.
mt: A number of cults offer you a merger, and if you refuse, you're going to be sorry.
en: Several cults propose merging with you. Refuse, and you'll hear some grumbling.

ko: 황금 촛대가 가득한 방이 완성되었습니다. 방에 들어선 신도들이 숨을 죽입니다.
mt: The room is full of golden candlesticks, and the crowd in the room is dying.
en: A room filled with golden candlesticks is complete. Followers hold their breath as they enter.

ko: 당신이 입은 옷을 따라 입는 신도가 늘었습니다.
mt: You've got a lot of people who wear what you wear.
en: More and more followers dress the way you do.

mt: Advanced wine storage has been donated.
en: A fine wine cellar has been donated.

ko: 부유한 사업가가 뒷자리에서 당신과 독대하기를 청합니다.
mt: A wealthy businessman asks to poison you in the back.
en: A wealthy businessman asks for a private audience with you, away from the crowd.

ko: 가난한 이들을 위한 무료 급식소를 엽니다. 역 앞까지 줄이 길게 이어집니다.
mt: Opens a free kitchen for the poor, and the line to the station is long.
en: You open a free soup kitchen for the poor. The line stretches all the way to the station.

ko: 절제의 서약을 맺은 신도들이 늘었습니다. 교단의 질서가 단단해집니다.
mt: A growing number of believers have taken vows to reform the order of the church.
en: More followers take vows of temperance. The cult's order grows firm.

ko: 병든 아이를 둔 어머니가 찾아와 무릎을 꿇습니다.
mt: The mother of a sick child comes and kneels down.
en: A mother with a sick child comes and falls to her knees.

mt: The two families where the gods quarreled are at peace.
en: Two feuding families among your followers reconcile.

ko: 버려진 아이들을 거두는 보육원 건립을 제안받습니다.
mt: It's proposed to set up a nursery for children who are abandoned.
en: You are asked to found an orphanage for abandoned children.

ko: 교단 회계를 공개하자는 목소리가 나옵니다. 신뢰가 쌓일 기회입니다.
mt: It's an opportunity to build trust.
en: Voices call for opening the cult's books. It's a chance to build trust.

ko: 오래 참고 기다린 신도가 마침내 믿음을 고백합니다.
mt: The faithful who have waited a long time finally confess their faith.
en: A follower who waited long and patiently finally professes his faith.

ko: 노동자들이 교단 농장에서 공정한 임금을 요구합니다. 당신은 이를 받아들입니다.
mt: Workers demand fair wages on school farms. You accept that.
en: Workers on the cult's farm demand fair wages. You agree.

ko: 청빈을 강조하자 신도들이 사치품을 스스로 내놓습니다.
mt: Let's highlight the poverty, and the faithful give their own luxuries.
en: When you preach honest poverty, your followers give up their luxuries of their own accord.

ko: 지역 병원에서 교단 자원봉사 요청이 옵니다.
mt: Local hospitals are asking us to volunteer for the school.
en: A local hospital asks the cult for volunteers.

ko: 한 신도가 전 재산을 교단에 맡기고 떠나며 말합니다. '나보다 더 가난한 이를 돌보시오.'
mt: A Shintoist leaves all his fortune to the church and says, "Look after someone who is poorer than I am."
en: A follower entrusts his entire fortune to the cult and leaves, saying, "Care for those poorer than I."

ko: 아프리카 가뭄 피해 마을에 우물을 파 주자는 제안이 나옵니다.
mt: There's a proposal to dig wells in the village from a drought in Africa.
en: Someone proposes digging wells for drought-stricken villages in Africa.

ko: 정직한 상인이 교단의 장부 감사를 자청합니다.
mt: An honest merchant offers to give thanks to the church's books.
en: An honest merchant volunteers to audit the cult's books.

ko: 어린 신도들이 찬송가를 지어 와 부릅니다. 맑은 목소리가 교회를 채웁니다.
mt: Young believers come and sing hymns. Clear voices fill the church.
en: Young followers write a hymn and sing it. Their clear voices fill the church.

ko: 교단 내 젊은 지도자가 자신의 자리를 양보하겠다고 나섭니다.
mt: My young leader says he's going to give up his position.
en: A young leader in the cult offers to step aside.

mt: The Tal North Korean family knocks on the door.
en: North Korean defector families knock on the cult's door.

ko: 학교 교사들이 교단 학교에서 무료로 가르치겠다고 합니다.
mt: School teachers say they're going to teach for free at a school.
en: Schoolteachers offer to teach for free at the cult's school.

ko: 오랜 병상의 신도가 완치되어 교단에 돌아옵니다. 모두가 기뻐합니다.
mt: The old sick man is cured and comes back to the church, and everybody's happy.
en: A long-bedridden follower returns to the cult fully healed. Everyone rejoices.

ko: 교단이 주최하는 바자회에서 수익금 전부가 고아원으로 갑니다.
mt: All the revenue goes to the orphanage at the barza party sponsored by the Faith.
en: All proceeds from the cult's bazaar go to an orphanage.

ko: 한 소녀가 찾아와 '당신을 믿고 싶다'고 말합니다. 당신은 조용히 손을 잡아 줍니다.
mt: A girl comes and says, "I want to trust you." You hold your hand quietly.
en: A girl comes and says, "I want to believe in you." You quietly take her hand.

ko: 새벽 기도 중 알 수 없는 낮은 목소리가 귀에 맴돕니다.
mt: There's an unknown low voice in your ear during the morning prayer.
en: During dawn prayer, a low, unknowable voice lingers in your ear.

ko: 오래된 성경 사본이 교단에 기증되었습니다. 여백에 누군가의 기도가 적혀 있습니다.
mt: An old copy of the Bible has been donated to the church, and in the margin is someone's prayer.
en: An old manuscript Bible is donated to the cult. Someone's prayer is written in its margins.

ko: 어린 시절 다니던 시골 교회가 문을 닫는다는 소식이 들립니다.
mt: We hear that our childhood rural church is closing down.
en: You hear that the country church you attended as a child is closing.

ko: 사흘 동안 금식하며 신의 뜻을 구하자는 생각이 듭니다.
mt: I have three days to fast and ask for God's will.
en: You feel the urge to fast for three days and seek God's will.

ko: 꿈에 하얀 옷을 입은 노인이 나타나 '아직 멀었다'고 말합니다.
mt: In my dream, an old man in white came up and said, "It's a long way off."
en: In a dream, an old man in white appears and says, "You are not there yet."

ko: 한 신도가 당신의 기도로 병이 나았다고 증언합니다.
mt: A Shintoist has testified that your prayers have healed him.
en: A follower testifies that your prayer healed him.

ko: 산속 기도원에서 일주일 머물라는 초대를 받았습니다.
mt: I was invited to stay a week at the mountain station.
en: You are invited to stay a week at a mountain prayer house.

ko: 라디오 설교자가 당신과 정반대의 교리를 열변합니다.
mt: A radio preacher is changing the very opposite of yours.
en: A radio preacher passionately expounds a doctrine opposite to yours.

ko: 폭우가 쏟아지는 밤, 번개가 교회 첨탑을 비켜 갑니다.
mt: A lightning bolt leaves the church steeple on a rainy night.
en: On a night of pouring rain, lightning spares the church spire.

ko: 오래 연락이 끊겼던 스승 목사가 병상에서 당신을 찾습니다.
mt: A long-lost teacher is looking for you on a sickbed.
en: Your old mentor pastor, long out of touch, asks for you from his sickbed.

ko: 성탄 전야, 홀로 빈 예배당에 앉아 있습니다.
mt: Before the Nativity, I'm sitting alone in an empty chapel.
en: On Christmas Eve, you sit alone in the empty chapel.

ko: 성경 구절 하나가 몇 주째 머릿속을 떠나지 않습니다.
mt: Every verse in the Bible has been in my head for weeks.
en: A single Bible verse hasn't left your mind for weeks.

ko: 교단 창립 기념일입니다. 처음 모였던 다섯 사람이 생각납니다.
mt: I remember the first five people I met.
en: It's the cult's founding anniversary. You remember the five people who first gathered.

ko: 한밤중 거리에서 술에 취한 청년이 당신에게 '신은 죽었다'고 외칩니다.
mt: In the middle of the night, a drunk young man cries out to you, 'God is dead.'
en: Late at night on the street, a drunk young man shouts at you, "God is dead!"

ko: 병원 원목실에서 임종 예배를 부탁해 왔습니다.
mt: I've been in the hospital's main office asking for my death prayer.
en: The hospital chaplaincy asks you to lead a deathbed service.

ko: 오랜 기도 끝에 손바닥에 알 수 없는 온기가 느껴집니다.
mt: After a long prayer, I feel an unknown warmth in the palm of my hand.
en: After long prayer, an inexplicable warmth fills your palms.

ko: 교단의 첫 성가집을 직접 엮어 보자는 생각이 떠오릅니다.
mt: It's the idea that we're going to put together the first choir of a cult.
en: You get the idea to compile the cult's first hymnal yourself.

ko: 가뭄이 길어지자 비를 내려 달라는 기도를 부탁받습니다.
mt: We're asked to ask for rain as soon as the drought lasts.
en: As the drought drags on, you are asked to pray for rain.

ko: 당신의 젊은 날 일기를 우연히 다시 읽게 됩니다.
mt: You'll be reading your youth's diary over and over again.
en: You happen to reread the diary of your youth.

ko: 주일 예배 중 한 신도가 감격에 겨워 쓰러집니다.
mt: One of the faithful of the week's service is overcome by emotion.
en: During Sunday service, a follower collapses, overcome with emotion.

ko: 신도 가정에 첫아이가 태어났습니다. 이름을 지어 달라고 합니다.
mt: The first child was born to a Shinto family, and he asked me to name him.
en: A follower family has had their first child. They ask you to name it.

ko: 신도들 사이에서 '교주님은 기도하지 않는다'는 뒷말이 돕니다.
mt: There's a saying among the believers that the Lord does not pray.
en: Whispers go around among your followers: "The leader doesn't pray."

ko: 신도 한 명이 사업이 망해 교회에 나오지 못하고 있습니다.
mt: One member of the congregation is not able to get to church because of the collapse of the business.
en: A follower's business has failed, and he has stopped coming to church.

ko: 청년부가 밤샘 찬양 집회를 열고 싶다고 합니다.
mt: He says he wants to hold a wake-up meeting.
en: The youth group wants to hold an all-night worship gathering.

ko: 노년 신도들이 젊은 사람들의 찬양 방식이 경박하다고 불평합니다.
mt: Old believers complain that the way young people celebrate is shallow.
en: Elderly followers complain the young people's worship style is frivolous.

ko: 한 신도가 가족의 반대로 세례를 미루고 있습니다.
mt: A Shintoist is putting off baptizing the other side of the family.
en: A follower is putting off baptism because her family objects.

mt: You have to decide where to spend the summer.
en: You must choose a location for the summer retreat.

ko: 신도가 꿈에서 계시를 받았다며 교단의 앞날을 예언합니다.
mt: I predict the future of the Faith, that the faithful are inspired in their dreams.
en: A follower claims a Revelation came to him in a dream and prophesies the cult's future.

ko: 성가대가 큰 대회에 나가고 싶어 합니다.
mt: The choir wants to go to a big contest.
en: The choir wants to enter a major competition.

ko: 신도들이 교주의 생일을 몰래 준비하고 있다는 것을 알게 됩니다.
mt: They find that the faithful are secretly preparing for the church's birthday.
en: You discover your followers are secretly planning your birthday.

mt: It's a proposal to create a bridge message.
en: Someone proposes a cult newsletter.

ko: 독감이 돌아 주일 예배 참석자가 반으로 줄었습니다.
mt: The flu fell and the weekly service attendance was cut in half.
en: A flu outbreak halves Sunday attendance.

ko: 가장 오래된 신도가 이사를 가게 되어 작별 인사를 왔습니다.
mt: The oldest Shintoist moved away and said goodbye.
en: Your oldest follower is moving away and comes to say goodbye.

ko: 신도 부부가 심하게 다투고 교회에서 서로를 피합니다.
mt: The congregation is very quarrelsome and avoids each other at church.
en: A married couple among your followers fights bitterly and avoids each other at church.

mt: There's not enough kids Sunday school teachers.
en: The children's Sunday school is short on teachers.

mt: They're saying, "Let's make a religion greeting."
en: Your followers want a greeting unique to the cult.

ko: 병든 노신도가 마지막으로 교주의 설교를 듣고 싶어 합니다.
mt: A sick old man wants to hear the last sermon of the dogma.
en: An ailing elderly follower wishes to hear your sermon one last time.

ko: 예배 후 식사 당번을 두고 신도들이 다툽니다.
mt: The congregation starts to argue after the service, after each meal.
en: Followers squabble over who's on meal duty after service.

ko: 교단 운영 위원회가 교주의 결정에 반대 의견을 냅니다.
mt: The school board of operations disagrees with the dogma's decision.
en: The cult's steering committee objects to your decision.

ko: 교주 전용 집무실을 만들자는 제안이 들어옵니다.
mt: There's a proposal to build a private office for the teacher.
en: Someone proposes a private office for the cult leader.

ko: 두 장로가 차기 지도자 자리를 두고 신경전을 벌입니다.
mt: Two elders take charge of a nervous conflict with the next leader.
en: Two elders jockey for the next leadership position.

ko: 교단의 정관을 문서로 정리할 때가 되었습니다.
mt: It's time for the Faith's Charter to be put into writing.
en: It's time to put the cult's bylaws in writing.

ko: 한 신도가 교주의 설교 내용을 공개적으로 반박합니다.
mt: A Shintoist publicly refutes the message of the dogma.
en: A follower publicly rebuts the content of your sermon.

ko: 지역 유지가 교단 행사에 상석을 요구합니다.
mt: Local maintenance demands an upper position at a school event.
en: A local bigwig demands the seat of honor at a cult event.

ko: 교단 내 직분 제도를 새로 만들자는 의견이 나옵니다.
mt: It's an idea to create a new institution for the Faith.
en: Someone suggests creating a new system of ranks in the cult.

ko: 교주의 차를 새로 사자는 안건이 올라왔습니다.
mt: A new message came up for a new teacher's car.
en: A motion is raised to buy the leader a new car.

ko: 교단 행사 중 마이크가 꺼져 당신의 목소리가 묻힙니다.
mt: Mike's off during the dogma. Your voice is buried.
en: During a cult event, the microphone cuts out and your voice is drowned.

ko: 교단 지도자 모임에서 당신을 '선생님'이 아닌 '교주님'으로 부르자는 말이 나옵니다.
mt: There's a group of religious leaders calling you "The Teacher," not "The Teacher."
en: At a leaders' meeting, someone suggests calling you not "Teacher" but "Cult Leader."

ko: 헌금 관리를 맡은 집사가 장부 공개를 거부합니다.
mt: The dean who is in charge of the collection refuses to release the books.
en: The deacon in charge of offerings refuses to open the books.

ko: 교주의 사진을 예배당에 걸자는 제안이 나옵니다.
mt: There's a proposal to put a picture of the dogma in the chapel.
en: Someone proposes hanging your photo in the chapel.

ko: 교단 휘장을 새로 디자인할 때가 되었습니다.
mt: It's time to redesign the school curtain.
en: It's time to redesign the cult's insignia.

ko: 젊은 전도사가 교주의 지시 없이 지부를 세웠습니다.
mt: A young preacher has set up a branch without instruction.
en: A young evangelist has founded a branch without your instruction.

ko: 교단 대표로 공청회에 나가 달라는 요청이 왔습니다.
mt: I've been asked to go to the public hearing as a representative of the Faith.
en: You are asked to represent the cult at a public hearing.

ko: 교단 내에서 교주 몰래 모이는 비밀 모임이 있다는 제보가 들어옵니다.
mt: There's a secret gathering within the cult.
en: A tip comes in about a secret group meeting behind your back within the cult.

ko: 신도들이 교주의 말을 녹음해 성구처럼 외우기 시작합니다.
mt: The faithful begin to record the sympathies and memorize them like scriptures.
en: Followers begin recording your words and memorizing them like scripture.

ko: 교단 행사의 사회자를 누구로 할지 두고 장로들이 다툽니다.
mt: The elders argue about who is the social leader of the cult event.
en: Elders squabble over who should emcee a cult event.

ko: 교단 창립자로서 자서전을 써 달라는 출판사의 제안이 들어옵니다.
mt: There's a publisher's offer to write a autobiography as the founder of the cult.
en: A publisher asks you, as the cult's founder, to write an autobiography.

ko: 추수감사절 헌금이 평소의 세 배나 걷혔습니다.
mt: The Thanksgiving contribution was three times the usual.
en: The Thanksgiving offering comes in at three times the usual amount.

ko: 신도 한 사람이 집을 팔아 헌금하겠다고 합니다.
mt: A faithful man offers to sell his house and contribute.
en: A follower says he will sell his house and give the money as an offering.

mt: In the contribution box, fake paper money was found.
en: Counterfeit bills turn up in the offering box.

ko: 교단 명의로 작은 서점을 열자는 제안이 나옵니다.
mt: It's suggested that we open a small bookstore in the name of the cult.
en: Someone proposes opening a small bookstore in the cult's name.

ko: 건설업자가 교단 부지에 큰 예배당을 지어 주겠다고 합니다.
mt: A contractor offers to build a large chapel in a church complex.
en: A builder offers to put up a large chapel on the cult's land.

ko: 헌금 바구니 대신 헌금 봉투를 쓰자는 의견이 나옵니다.
mt: Instead of a basket, we're going to have to write a contribution envelope.
en: Someone suggests using offering envelopes instead of baskets.

ko: 교단 바자회를 열어 기금을 모으자는 제안이 나옵니다.
mt: It's suggested that we hold a school bar and raise the fund.
en: Someone proposes a cult bazaar to raise funds.

mt: The faithful are curious about where the contributions are being spent.
en: Your followers wonder where their offerings go.

ko: 은행에서 교단 자금을 예금하면 높은 이자를 주겠다고 합니다.
mt: Banks will give you high interest if you deposit the money.
en: A bank offers high interest if the cult deposits its funds there.

mt: This year's harvest is abundant on the school farm.
en: The cult farm's harvest is bountiful this year.

ko: 부유한 신도가 큰 헌금과 함께 장로 자리를 원합니다.
mt: A wealthy believer wants to be an elder with a large contribution.
en: A wealthy follower wants an elder's seat in exchange for a large offering.

ko: 교회 종을 녹여 팔면 큰돈이 된다는 고물상이 찾아옵니다.
mt: And when you melt church bells and sell them, they come back to you, and they're going to make a lot of money.
en: A scrap dealer comes by, saying the church bell would fetch a fortune melted down.

ko: 교단 인쇄물 비용이 너무 많이 든다는 보고가 올라옵니다.
mt: There's a report that it costs too much to print.
en: A report comes in that the cult's printing costs are far too high.

ko: 헌금 담당 집사가 헌금 일부를 빌려 쓰다 걸렸습니다.
mt: It took the director of the collection to borrow some of the contributions.
en: The deacon in charge of offerings is caught borrowing from them.

ko: 교단 기금으로 장학금을 만들자는 의견이 나옵니다.
mt: The idea is to make scholarships for the school fund.
en: Someone suggests creating a scholarship from cult funds.

ko: 이웃 교회가 경영난으로 교단 건물을 싸게 팔겠다고 합니다.
mt: The neighboring church says they're going to sell the school building cheaply for management reasons.
en: A struggling neighboring church offers to sell you its building cheap.

mt: The Christmas contribution was less than expected.
en: The Christmas offering falls short of expectations.

ko: 교단 앞 빈 땅에 주차장을 만들면 수입이 생긴다는 제안이 나옵니다.
mt: You can build a parking lot in the open ground in front of the school, and you get an offer.
en: Someone suggests turning the empty lot in front of the cult into a paid parking lot.

ko: 오래된 신도가 유언으로 교단에 땅을 남겼습니다.
mt: An old Shinto left land in the pulpit by will.
en: A longtime follower has left the cult land in his will.

ko: 시장 한복판에서 전도를 하자는 제안이 나옵니다.
mt: In the middle of the market, there's a proposal to preach.
en: Someone proposes evangelizing in the middle of the market.

ko: 대학가에 교단 동아리를 만들자는 의견이 나옵니다.
mt: We're going to make a school club in a college district.
en: Someone suggests starting a cult club in the college district.

ko: 신도 한 사람이 친구 열 명을 데려오겠다고 큰소리칩니다.
mt: One of them shouts out that he's going to bring in ten friends.
en: A follower boasts he will bring ten friends.

ko: 다른 교회에서 상처받은 신도들이 무리 지어 찾아옵니다.
mt: A group of injured members from other churches come.
en: Followers hurt by other churches arrive in a group.

ko: 신문 광고로 교단을 알리자는 제안이 나옵니다.
mt: There's a proposal to make the Church known by newspaper advertising.
en: Someone proposes advertising the cult in the newspaper.

ko: 공장 노동자들이 퇴근 후 모일 곳이 없다고 합니다.
mt: There's no place for factory workers to gather after work.
en: Factory workers say they have nowhere to gather after work.

ko: 신도들이 이웃 마을에 교단 소개 모임을 열자고 합니다.
mt: A group of believers in a neighboring village wants to hold an introduction meeting for the church.
en: Your followers want to hold an introductory meeting in the next village.

ko: 교회 앞에서 무료로 차를 나누자는 아이디어가 나옵니다.
mt: We have the idea of sharing a car for free in front of a church.
en: Someone has the idea of handing out free tea outside the church.

mt: There's an opinion from the revivalist.
en: Someone suggests inviting a revival speaker.

ko: 이사 온 가족이 교회를 찾고 있다는 소식을 듣습니다.
mt: We hear that the whole family is looking for a church.
en: You hear that a family that just moved in is looking for a church.

ko: 청소년들이 교회 마당에서 축구를 하고 싶어 합니다.
mt: Young people want to play football in the church yard.
en: Teenagers want to play soccer in the churchyard.

ko: 외국인 노동자들이 교단 예배에 관심을 보입니다.
mt: Foreign workers are interested in the services of the Faith.
en: Migrant workers show interest in the cult's services.

ko: 교단 신도 수를 세어 보니 지난해보다 줄었습니다.
mt: The number of cults was lower than last year.
en: A head count shows fewer followers than last year.

ko: 교단 이름이 어렵다며 바꾸자는 의견이 나옵니다.
mt: It's hard to name a cult, so there's an opinion to change.
en: Someone suggests changing the cult's name because it's hard to say.

ko: 지역 축제에 교단 부스를 차리자는 제안이 들어옵니다.
mt: There's a proposal to set up a school booth at the local festival.
en: You are invited to set up a cult booth at the local festival.

ko: 교단에 등록만 하고 나오지 않는 신도가 많습니다.
mt: There's a lot of people who just sign up for the Faith and don't come out.
en: Many followers register with the cult but never show up.

ko: 버스 정류장 앞에 교단 안내판을 세우자는 의견이 나옵니다.
mt: In front of the bus stop, we're going to set up a school board.
en: Someone suggests putting up a cult sign at the bus stop.

ko: 신도들의 가족 초청 주일을 열자는 제안이 나옵니다.
mt: It's suggested that we hold a family week of believers.
en: Someone proposes a family-invitation Sunday for followers.

ko: 병원 앞에서 환자 가족들을 위한 기도 천막을 세우자는 의견이 나옵니다.
mt: In front of the hospital, we're going to set up a prayer tent for the family.
en: Someone suggests pitching a prayer tent for patients' families outside the hospital.

mt: We're going to make a catechism.
en: Someone suggests writing a Doctrine catechism.

ko: 신학생이 교단의 교리에 날카로운 질문을 던집니다.
mt: A new student asks a sharp question to the dogma of the Faith.
en: A seminary student poses sharp questions about your Doctrine.

ko: 교단 교리를 한 문장으로 정리하자는 제안이 나옵니다.
mt: It's suggested that we put the dogma into one sentence.
en: Someone proposes summing up the Doctrine in a single sentence.

mt: I think about the original Bible language.
en: You consider learning the Bible's original languages.

ko: 교리를 두고 신도 둘이 심하게 다툽니다.
mt: They're both very serious about doctrine.
en: Two followers quarrel bitterly over the Doctrine.

ko: 오래된 교부들의 글을 번역해 신도들에게 읽히자는 의견이 나옵니다.
mt: It's an idea to translate the writings of the old Fathers and read them to the faithful.
en: Someone suggests translating the Church Fathers for your followers to read.

ko: 어린이를 위한 교리 그림책을 만들자는 제안이 나옵니다.
mt: It's suggested that we create a doctrinal picture book for children.
en: Someone proposes a Doctrine picture book for children.

ko: 교단의 예배 순서를 새로 정비할 때가 되었습니다.
mt: It's time to renovate the order of the cult's services.
en: It's time to overhaul the cult's order of worship.

ko: 신도 교육용 성경 공부 과정을 만들자는 의견이 나옵니다.
mt: It turns out that we're going to build a program of Bible study for education.
en: Someone suggests a Bible study course to educate followers.

ko: 교리에 맞지 않는 민간 풍습을 따르는 신도들이 있습니다.
mt: There are members of the community who do not adhere to doctrine.
en: Some followers keep folk customs at odds with the Doctrine.

ko: 신학교 교수가 교단의 교리를 연구하고 싶다며 찾아옵니다.
mt: A professor of theology comes to me, wanting to study the dogma of the Faith.
en: A seminary professor visits, wanting to study your Doctrine.

ko: 교주의 설교를 녹음해 CD로 배포하자는 의견이 나옵니다.
mt: We're going to record a teacher's sermon and distribute it to a CD.
en: Someone suggests recording your sermons and distributing them on CD.

ko: 교리 시험을 통과해야 직분을 주자는 제안이 나옵니다.
mt: It's a proposal to pass a doctrinal test to give you an office.
en: Someone proposes that ranks be granted only after passing a Doctrine exam.

ko: 오랜 세월 써 온 기도문에 오래된 표현이 많습니다.
mt: There's a lot of old expressions in prayers that have been written for a long time.
en: The prayers used for years are full of archaic phrasing.

ko: 교단의 교리를 영어로 옮겨 해외에 알리자는 의견이 나옵니다.
mt: Let's move the dogma of the Faith to English, and let's make it known abroad.
en: Someone suggests translating the Doctrine into English to spread it abroad.

ko: 교리 묵상 일지를 쓰게 하자는 제안이 나옵니다.
mt: It's suggested that we use a doctrinal meditation journal.
en: Someone proposes having followers keep Doctrine meditation journals.

ko: 이단 시비를 피하려면 교리를 명확히 하라는 조언을 듣습니다.
mt: If you're going to avoid Ethan Shibby, you're going to be advised to clarify the doctrine.
en: You are advised to clarify the Doctrine to avoid charges of heresy.

ko: 설교 준비를 도울 조수를 두자는 의견이 나옵니다.
mt: Let's have an assistant to help prepare for the sermon.
en: Someone suggests getting an assistant to help prepare sermons.

mt: It's suggested that we build a school library.
en: Someone proposes a cult library.

mt: The faithful are asking us to dress up together.
en: Your followers want to make kimchi together.

ko: 예배 후 함께 식사하는 전통을 만들자는 의견이 나옵니다.
mt: We're going to make a tradition of having a meal together after a service.
en: Someone suggests a tradition of eating together after service.

ko: 신도들끼리 서로의 집을 돌며 기도하는 모임을 만들자고 합니다.
mt: Let's have a group of believers going around each other in prayer.
en: Your followers want a group that prays in each other's homes in turn.

ko: 신도 한 사람이 화재로 집을 잃었습니다.
mt: One of the gods lost his house in a fire.
en: A follower has lost his home in a fire.

ko: 교회 창고를 정리하다 오래된 사진첩이 나왔습니다.
mt: An old photo album came out of organizing a church warehouse.
en: Clearing out the church storeroom, you find an old photo album.

mt: The believers are asking us to go up in the mountains together.
en: Your followers want to go hiking together.

ko: 두 구역 모임이 사소한 일로 사이가 틀어졌습니다.
mt: The two district meetings got a little bit out of the way.
en: Two cell groups have fallen out over something trivial.

ko: 신도들이 교단 합창단을 만들고 싶어 합니다.
mt: The faithful want to create a cult choir.
en: Your followers want to form a cult choir.

ko: 명절에 고향에 가지 못하는 신도들이 많습니다.
mt: There's a lot of believers who don't go home on holidays.
en: Many followers can't go home for the holidays.

ko: 신도들 사이에 험담이 돈다는 이야기가 들립니다.
mt: You hear that there's gossip amongst the faithful.
en: You hear that gossip is circulating among your followers.

ko: 신도들이 서로의 기도 제목을 나누는 시간을 갖자고 합니다.
mt: Let the faithful have time to share the title of each other's prayers.
en: Your followers want time to share their prayer requests.

ko: 교단 창립 이래 처음으로 신도들끼리 결혼식을 올립니다.
mt: For the first time since the founding of the cult, the faithful have held their own weddings.
en: For the first time since the cult's founding, two followers are marrying each other.

ko: 신도들이 함께 농사지을 텃밭을 만들자고 합니다.
mt: A group of believers are saying, "Let's make a garden for the land.
en: Your followers want to start a shared vegetable garden.

ko: 오랜 신도가 다른 신도에게 돈을 빌려주고 받지 못했습니다.
mt: The old Shinto didn't lend money to other members.
en: A longtime follower lent money to another and was never repaid.

ko: 청년들과 노인들이 서로 대화가 없다는 지적이 나옵니다.
mt: It turns out that young and old don't talk to each other.
en: Someone points out that the young and old never talk to each other.

ko: 교회 대청소 날을 정하자는 의견이 나옵니다.
mt: It's a question of the day of church cleansing.
en: Someone suggests setting a day for cleaning the whole church.

ko: 추운 겨울, 연탄이 부족한 신도 가정들이 있습니다.
mt: In cold winters, there are Shinto families that lack fuel.
en: In the cold of winter, some follower households are short on coal.

ko: 신도들이 서로 이름을 모른다는 이야기가 나옵니다.
